summary: A merge conflict happens when two branches change the same lines. Git stops, marks both versions in the file, and waits for you to choose.
notes: Between <<<<<<< HEAD and ======= is your branch's version. Between ======= and >>>>>>> is the other branch's version.
Delete all three marker lines and leave the text you want. In an editor, this is the same edit done by hand.
git merge --abort cancels the merge and puts everything back the way it was before.
pitfall: Committing a file that still has <<<<<<< in it saves the markers into your code, and Python reports SyntaxError. Run cat or git diff to check before git add.
setup_note: Starts on main. main changed Liam's score to 94, and the branch retake-scores changed the same line to 97.
setup:
cat > gradebook.py <<'EOF'
scores = [88, 92, 79, 95]
average = sum(scores) / len(scores)
print("Average:", average)
EOF

cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# Gradebook
Quiz scores for Period 3.
EOF

cat > scores.csv <<'EOF'
name,score
Ava,88
Liam,92
Noah,79
Zoe,95
EOF
git add -A && git commit -q -m "Add quiz scores"
git add -A && git commit -q -m "Record Liam's retake score"
git add -A && git commit -q -m "Fix Liam's score"
